approvedDesignText:
Add repeatable `--field <name>` and repeatable `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. The two forms are mutually exclusive; combining them fails before any project request. Either selection form combined with `--format` also fails before any project request, preserving all formatted/JSON output behavior.

Without either new flag, table, JSON, query behavior, field-query behavior, pagination, and legacy table bytes remain unchanged. With a selection flag, the normal table retains its existing `Type`, `Title`, `Number`, `Repository`, and `ID` columns unchanged, then appends one column per requested selection in exactly request order. Repeating a selection within one form produces repeated columns; no deduplication occurs. Column headers use the resolved project field names.

The regular item-list query already fetches the first project-field page and each item’s typed field values. For a selected-field invocation, if `project.Fields.PageInfo.HasNextPage` is false, resolve exclusively against those returned definitions, adding no request. If it is true, request only subsequent field pages beginning at that returned end cursor, append them to the first page, and continue until all field pages are collected. This continuation must be limited to field-selection invocations; it must not refetch the initial field page or run at all without a selection flag. It must complete successfully before resolving or rendering: any continuation error returns a useful error and emits no table rows or partial table.

Resolve each requested name case-insensitively and each ID exactly against the complete field list. An unknown name error explicitly shows all available field names in deterministic lexical order. An unknown ID error explicitly shows all available `name (id)` candidates in deterministic lexical order. An ambiguous case-insensitive name error explicitly lists the matching IDs in deterministic lexical order and tells the user to use `--field-id`. Resolve selected fields before checking for no items, so invalid selections never become a misleading empty-result response.

For every listed item, locate a selected field’s value by field ID. Absent values render as an empty cell. Render date and text values directly; numbers in compact decimal form; single-select values by option name; iterations and milestones by title; labels, users, reviewers, and pull requests as `, `-joined names/logins/URLs; and repository values as URLs. For these newly rendered selected-field values only, remove carriage returns and replace newlines with spaces before table rendering. Unknown field-value variants render as empty cells. Legacy table cells and headers are never normalized or otherwise changed on invocations without the new flags. Add focused tests covering flag parsing, mutual exclusions, case-insensitive matching, deterministic missing/ambiguous diagnostics, no-extra-request resolution, conditional full field pagination including failure-before-render, requested column ordering/repetition, selected-value normalization, empty values, all supported value renderings, and unchanged existing output.
